HOW IT WORKS

Move from business records to useful insight

Sales and stock reports bring everyday transaction and item records into one selected reporting period. Instead of reviewing invoices one by one, you can compare product activity, understand stock position, and investigate the records behind important changes.

01

Choose a meaningful period

Use a preset or custom date range that matches the business question you want to answer.

02

Review sales performance

Compare product-level sales activity and examine net and gross values for the selected period.

03

Check inventory position

Review current quantities, inventory value, and products approaching their reorder level.

04

Investigate the underlying records

Open the relevant product, customer, invoice, or stock record before making a pricing, purchasing, or follow-up decision.

KEY CAPABILITIES

See the numbers behind sales and inventory

Product-level sales

See which products or services generated sales during the selected period.

Net and gross comparison

Review values before and after applicable tax to understand reported totals.

Inventory value

Monitor the recorded value represented by stock currently held.

Top-performing items

Identify products contributing the strongest sales activity or volume.

Leading customers

See which customers are associated with the highest sales totals.

Flexible date filtering

Use preset and custom periods for consistent, meaningful comparisons.

WHY IT MATTERS

Use reporting to make better operating decisions

Useful reporting connects sales activity with inventory position. It helps you understand what sold, what remains in stock, and which underlying records deserve closer attention.

01

Recognize product demand

Product-level sales reveal which items are contributing revenue and which may require a pricing, promotion, or purchasing review.

02

Protect stock availability

Current quantities, inventory value, and reorder context help reduce avoidable stockouts or unnecessary purchasing.

03

Make decisions from evidence

Date filters and underlying records provide context before you act on an unusual total, leading customer, or changing sales pattern.

PRACTICAL CHECKLIST

Use understand sales and stock well

  • Compare equivalent date ranges whenever possible.
  • Confirm tax treatment before interpreting net and gross values.
  • Investigate the invoices and items behind unusual report totals.
  • Reconcile operational inventory value with your formal accounting method.
Always confirm the legal, tax, and record-keeping requirements that apply to your business.

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Questions about understand sales and stock

Can I review sales by product?

Yes. Product-level reporting helps you compare sales activity, quantities, and values for the selected reporting period.

What is the difference between net and gross sales?

Net generally represents the value before applicable tax, while gross includes applicable tax. Confirm the active tax configuration and report definitions before relying on a comparison.

How is inventory value used?

Inventory value provides an operational summary of the recorded stock position. It can support purchasing and stock-review decisions but should be reconciled with the accounting method used by your business.

Can I identify top-selling products and customers?

The reporting workflow highlights leading items and customers so you can investigate the records contributing to those totals.

Why should I compare date ranges?

Consistent date ranges help reveal changes in product demand, customer activity, sales value, and inventory position without mixing incomparable periods.

Are the figures shown on this page real customer data?

No. All names, quantities, and financial values shown in marketing visuals are fictional demonstration data.
